senses.gloss:
√stigh (stiñnóti). proceed, stride; esp.
proceed against, attack. [cf. στείχω,
‘proceed, march, go in line,’ rarely
‘mount up’; Church Slavonic stignati,
‘hasten’: the root is wide-spread in Germanic,
 but often shows a specialization of
mg, ‘proceed upward, ascend, climb’; cf.
AS. stīg-an, which often means simply
‘proceed, go,’ but also ‘ascendere,’ and
even ‘descendere’; Ger. steig-en, ‘mount
up’; AS. stǣg-er, ‘a step to climb by,’
Eng. stair; AS. stigel, ‘step or steps for
climbing over a fence,’ Eng. stile; AS.
stig-rāp, stī-rāp, ‘mounting-rope,’ Eng.
stirrup; Ger. Steg-reif, ‘stirrup’; AS.
[]
stīgend, ‘rising or sty,’ Eng. sty, ‘swelling
(on eye-lid)’: for change of gh to ñ in
present, cf. 161^1 and^4.]
+ pra, get ahead in attacking, succeed
in one's attacks, 935, 10, 11.
